Content:
Let's take a look at the following graph of the function [MATH: f(x)=\sqrt{x}] and its tangent line [MATH: \color{orange} L] at [MATH: x=4.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/bfac83170db6a25e3cabf8db55996d97]

Content:
From this graph, we can see that near [MATH: x=4,] the tangent line and the function are very close to each other. So, the line [MATH: L(x)] is a good approximation of the function for points close to [MATH: x=4.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/abb360e16b5be46062da69c4a8129917]

Content:
Here, the tangent line approximation of the function [MATH: f(x)=\sqrt{x}] at the point [MATH: a=4] is defined by
[MATH: L(x) = f(4) + f^{′}(4)(x − 4).]

Content:
Let's calculate [MATH: f(4)] and [MATH: f'(4)] in the expression above. Evaluating the function at [MATH: a=4,] we get

Content:
[MATH: f(4) = \sqrt{4} = 2,]
and computing the derivative, we get
[MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (d)/(dx)(sqrt(x)); = (d)/(dx)(x^{1/2}); = (1)/(2sqrt(x)),]
which in turn gives
[MATH: f'(4) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{1}{4}.]

Content:
Finally, we obtain
[MATH: L(x)|= f(4) + f^{′}(4)(x − 4); = 2 + (1)/(4)(x − 4); = 2 + (1)/(4)x − 1; = (1)/(4)x + 1.]

items.title: Estimating the Square Root of a Number Using a Tangent Line Approximation

sections.normalized_html: Approximate the value of [MATH: \sqrt{49.1}] using the tangent line approximation of [MATH: f(x)=\sqrt{x}] at [MATH: x=49.]
sections.readable_text: Approximate the value of [MATH: \sqrt{49.1}] using the tangent line approximation of [MATH: f(x)=\sqrt{x}] at [MATH: x=49.]

sections.normalized_html:
The tangent line approximation of [MATH: f(x)] at the point [MATH: x = a] is

[MATH: L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a)]

In our case, we have [MATH: a=49,] which gives

[MATH: L(x) = f(49) + f^{′}(49)(x − 49).]

Let's compute [MATH: f(49)] and [MATH: f'(49)] in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get [MATH: f\left( 49\right) = \sqrt{49}= 7,] and computing the derivative, we get [MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (d)/(dx)(sqrt(x)) = (1)/(2sqrt(x)),] which in turn gives [MATH: f'\left( 49\right) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{49}} = \dfrac{1}{2\cdot 7} = \dfrac{1}{14}.]

So, the tangent line approximation is [MATH: L(x) = 7 + (1)/(14)(x − 49).]

We can approximate [MATH: \sqrt{49.1}] by evaluating the tangent line approximation at [MATH: x=49.1.] We get [MATH: sqrt(49.1)|≈ L(49.1); = 7 + (1)/(14)(49.1 − 49); = 7 + (1)/(14)(0.1); = 7 + (1)/(14)((1)/(10)); = 7 + (1)/(140); = (981)/(140); ≈ 7.007143.]

Note that the exact answer, rounded to six decimal places, is [MATH: \sqrt{49.1} = 7.007\,139.] Our approximation is very close!

Explanation:
The tangent line approximation of [MATH: f(x)] at the point [MATH: x = a] is

[MATH: L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a)]

In our case, we have [MATH: a=8,] which gives

[MATH: L(x) = f(8) + f^{′}(8)(x − 8).]

Let's compute [MATH: f(8)] and [MATH: f'(8)] in the expression above. Evaluating the function at [MATH: a=8,] we get
[MATH: f(8) = \sqrt[3]{8} = 2,]
and computing the derivative, we get
[MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (d)/(dx)(root(x, 3)); = (d)/(dx)(x^{1/3}); = (1)/(3root(x^{2}, 3)),]
which in turn,gives
[MATH: f'(8) = \dfrac{1}{3\left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^2} = \dfrac{1}{12}.]

So the tangent line approximation is

[MATH: L(x) = 2 + \dfrac{1}{12}(x-8).]

We can approximate [MATH: \sqrt[3]{9}] by evaluating the tangent line approximation at [MATH: x=9.] We get
